title: Multi-tenant hit-ensemble: TTL/policy recommendations + guarded apply harness
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Goal: Ship a production-ready service that recommends per-tenant and per-prefix KV cache TTL and policy changes using a hit-rate ensemble model, plus an automated guarded-apply harness (dry-run, shadow, staged apply, automatic rollback) to minimize cost while protecting latency SLOs and cache correctness.

Why now: Several customers and internal tenants show 10-30% token cost variance caused by suboptimal prefix TTLs and inconsistent cache key shaping. Manual tuning is error-prone and risky at scale. This ticket builds the modeling + safety automation needed for safe rollouts.

Scope:
- Hit-rate ensemble model that combines: LRU-driven simulation, Bayesian shrinkage per-prefix, and short-window time-series forecasting to predict marginal hit-change for TTL adjustments.
- Recommendation engine that outputs: suggested TTL delta (seconds), candidate eviction policy (ttl-based vs size-based), and suggested key transforms (trim suffixes, canonicalize numeric ids).
- Guarded apply harness: shadow/dry-run mode, staged rollout controller (cohorts by traffic slices), automatic rollback triggers based on metrics (hit-rate drop, tail-latency increase, error spike), and post-apply validation.
- Integration points: Console recommendations UI (follow-up PM ticket), runtime rollout API, and Redwood monitoring (dashboards + trace links).

Non-goals: Full UI design, manual opps runbook (we provide automation + runbook skeleton only).

Acceptance criteria:
1) Model consistently predicts hit-rate delta within +/- 5 percentage points on the historical backtest across 3 production tenants (sampled).
2) Recommendation engine produces a consumable JSON spec (keys: prefix, old_ttl, recommended_ttl, expected_hit_delta, confidence) and an explanation string for each recommendation.
3) Guarded apply harness can perform dry-run and shadow apply with no traffic impact, and complete a staged rollout with automatic rollback on defined triggers.
4) End-to-end test and a chaos test that simulates a mis-keying change ensure automatic rollback triggers fire in < 5 minutes.
5) PRs with implementation and unit/integration tests merged and feature flagged behind optimize-2.4.

Metrics to monitor (linked dashboards below):
- Per-prefix hit-rate, global KV hit-rate, per-tenant token cost, p99 generation latency, cache miss amplification (requests per miss).
- Safety metrics: rollback count, false-positive rollback rate, time-to-rollback.

Artifacts and links:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Multi-tenant+Hit-Ensemble+Design (internal)
- Modeling notebook (backtest): https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-notebooks/pull/134 (notebook + sample outputs)
- GH PR (guarded apply prototype): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2894
- Dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/kv-hit-ensemble/kv-hit-ensemble-overview
implementation_plan:
Phase 1 (2 weeks): build offline modeling pipeline + backtests. Deliverables: model artifacts, notebook, and API that returns prediction for a tenant/prefix window.
Phase 2 (2 weeks): recommendation engine + spec format. Deliverables: recommendation JSON schema, CLI tool to generate batched recommendations, unit tests.
Phase 3 (3 weeks): guarded apply harness + staged rollout controller. Deliverables: dry-run/shadow modes, cohort rollout controller, rollback triggers, integration tests.
Phase 4 (1 week): end-to-end canary on internal tenants, monitoring dashboard tiles, runbook.

Safety gates: start with non-customer production tenants, 1% traffic cohort, require two engineer approvals to move to 10% and 100%. All changes behind feature flag.
test_plan: Unit tests for prediction logic and recommendation serializer. Integration tests: shadow apply that validates no changes to live KV behavior. E2E: simulate TTL change that intentionally mis-canonicalizes a prefix to validate rollback. Load test to measure latency impact at 10k rps.
acceptance_criteria: See description section; must meet model accuracy, recommendation schema, guarded apply behavior, and chaos rollback tests before closing.
